newsitem.title: UK: UK lead concentrations in blood fall markedly.
newsitem.headline: UK lead concentrations in blood fall markedly.

text.p: Lead concentrations in the blood of Britons has fallen substantially since the mid-1980s, research released on Friday showed.
Researchers writing in the British Medical Journal said blood samples were collected in 1995 from 6,868 people considered to be a representative sample of the whole population.
"The concentrations that we found recently are much lower than those found in the environmental programmes in the United Kingdom in 1984-7," the letter to the journal said.

The samples showed that 97 percent of Britons who were exposed only to environmental sources of lead had blood lead concentrations below the action limit of 0.48 micrograms per decilitre operating in other countries.
Samples were taken from people living in traffic-heavy areas and in areas without heavy traffic.
"Since 1984-7, blood lead concentrations have fallen by a factor of 2.6-3.0 in adults and by a factor of 3.6-5.0 in children," they said.
A number of measures was introduced in Britain in the 1980s to reduce lead in the environment because of worries over its effect on children and their development.
Lead solder was removed from tins containing food, lead in paint was controlled and lead in petrol was reduced.
